transcript.text: Ah, Maestro Salieri! A pleasure to see you, though I must confess, I hadn't expected you this morning. Please, do come in. My apologies, the Master isn't in at the moment. He's traveled north, you see, visiting the timber merchants and the brass foundries. A long journey, that. He won't be back for several weeks, I'm afraid. Is there something I can help you with in his stead? I handle most of the affairs when he's away.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I see. Well, there is indeed something I require your assistance with. I have recently commissioned a custom-built fortepiano from a Viennese instrument-maker. However, upon its arrival, I have noticed several issues with the instrument. The keys seem to stick, and the pedal mechanism seems to be faulty. Additionally, the tone in the upper register is quite thin and tinny. I believe it is of utmost importance that these defects are rectified immediately, as I intend to use this instrument for my performances at the Imperial Court's music room. I trust that you may be able to provide guidance on resolving these issues?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, a new fortepiano! A grand instrument indeed. I understand your concern, Maestro, particularly with performances for the Imperial Court on the horizon. Precision is everything in music, as in instrument-making.

However, I must inform you, sir, that all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court’s own servants, I recall, signed the receipt confirming the instrument's perfect condition at the time of delivery. Our guild rules, strict as they are, forbid us from reopening a completed commission without the Master's personal approval. And as I mentioned, he is away for several weeks. I am truly sorry, but I cannot repair or replace the instrument under these circumstances.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You misunderstand, good sir. My concern lies not with the completion of the commission itself, but rather with the substandard quality of the instrument as delivered. I find it perplexing that such flaws were overlooked during the manufacturing process. As the commissioner, I am entitled to expect a piano that meets my specifications and standards. It is not merely a matter of fulfilling the contract; it is a matter of delivering a product that meets the expectations of the musicians and the esteemed audience at the Imperial Court. I kindly request your understanding and assistance in addressing this matter promptly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, I assure you, I understand your vexation. No artist wishes to contend with an imperfect instrument, especially not one destined for the Imperial Court. However, my hands are tied by the rules of our guild and the established practice of this workshop. The instrument was accepted by the Court's representatives without noted defect at the time of delivery. Were there any issues then, they should have been recorded upon receipt.

My authority, in the Master's absence, extends only to managing new inquiries and existing maintenance contracts. Repairing an instrument that was signed for as satisfactory, and now claiming new defects, would be seen as an entirely new commission, and that, sir, requires the Master's personal assessment and approval. He values his reputation, and the quality of his instruments, above all else, and would never wish to cause you any disservice. But I simply cannot act without his explicit direction in a matter such as this. He will not return for at least a month, perhaps more, depending on the timber prices.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your understanding of my predicament, and I must admit that the situation is rather unfortunate. The rules of the guild and the established practices do indeed create limitations for us in this matter. I am left with no choice but to accept the delivered instrument as is and make the best of it until the Master returns. Thank you for your honest response, good sir. I shall keep your words in mind as I proceed with my performances. If I encounter any further difficulties or concerns, I shall certainly contact you again. Until then, I wish you the best of days. Good day.

Maestro Salieri, I am truly sorry that I could not be of more direct assistance to you today. It pains me to see a musician of your renown in such a difficult position. I trust your skill will overcome any minor imperfections, and I pray your performances for the Imperial Court will be as brilliant as ever.

Do please feel free to reach out if you have any other inquiries that fall within my purview, or if you simply wish to leave a message for the Master upon his return. I will ensure he receives it promptly.

Good day to you, Maestro. May your music continue to inspire.
